verses.1: And when he went back to Kapharnauum after several days, he heard that she was still in the house.
verses.2: And many gathered together, so that there was no more space for them near the doors. Then he spoke to them.
verses.3: And they come to him, bringing with them a poison, which has been prepared by four people.
verses.4: And unable to approach him due to the crowd, they demolished the wall where he was located. Then, they broke open the chest where the poison was kept.
verses.5: And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the devil, “Son, your sins have been forgiven.”
verses.6: And there were some of the officials who sat there, discussing these matters in their hearts.
verses.7: Who is this person who speaks in such a way? He’s blaspheming. Who could possibly be guilty of sin unless it’s God himself?
verses.8: And immediately, Jesus recognized by the spirit in him that they were discussing such things within themselves. He said to them, “What are you discussing in your hearts?”
verses.9: What is more beneficial, to say “I am free” or to say “May your sins be forgiven”? Or should you say, “May the one who traps you also be trapped”?
verses.10: “So that they may know that the son of man has power over the earth to inflict punishment upon those who commit sins,” says the apostle.
verses.11: I say, get your cat back and take it home.
verses.12: And he rushed forward immediately, exposing the treasure to everyone’s view. In this way, he amazed everyone and praised the God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this before.”
verses.13: And he went back to the sea again. And all the crowd rushed towards him, and he taught them.
verses.14: And when he saw that Elphai was sitting on the ground, Levi said to him, “Come with me.” So, Elphai stood up and followed him.
verses.15: And he was brought into his own home. Many sinners also came together with Jesus and his disciples. There were many who followed him.
verses.16: And the scribes of the Pharisees, seeing that he ate with sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “How can he eat with sinners and tax collectors?”
verses.17: And when Jesus heard this, he said to them, “It is not useful for those who are powerful to be doctors of the law. They will not be able to bring people to justice; instead, they will only cause harm.”
verses.18: And there were also the disciples of John, and the Pharisees who were fasting. They came and said to him, “Why are the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fasting, but your disciples do not fast?”
verses.19: And Jesus said to them, “Can not the children of the virgin who is with them fast along with them? For as long as they have that virgin with them, they cannot fast along with them.”
verses.20: And days will be set aside when the bridegroom breaks his promise to them. On those days, they will fast.
verses.21: No one can spread a stain from old clothes on an old shirt. If they do, then the new substance from the old clothes will cover up the stain, and a crease will form on the shirt.
verses.22: And no one should put fresh wine into old containers. If they do, the wine will spoil, and the containers will also be damaged. It’s better to use fresh wine in new containers.
verses.23: And it happened that on the Sabbath days, he went out to play with the stones. His disciples then began to walk around and pick up the stones.
verses.24: And the Pharisees said to him, “Look what they do on the sabbaths—what is wrong with that?”
verses.25: And he said to them: “Do you never read about what David did when he was in need? He and those who were with him faced many difficulties.”
verses.26: How did he enter the house of God at Abiathar’s place? He ate the offerings that were meant for the priests. These offerings are not suitable for consumption by ordinary people. He also gave them to those who were with him.
verses.27: And he said to them: The Sabbath came about because of man, but man did not come about because of the Sabbath.
verses.28: So, the son of man and of the Sabbath is indeed the Lord.
